# SSGOI setup guide

SSGOI adds route transitions without replacing the application router.

Current core version: `@ssgoi/core@7.0.0-beta.2`

## Contents

1. Next.js setup
2. Route boundaries and React lifetime
3. Persistent layouts
4. Sliding tabs
5. Bottom navigation and route groups
6. Transition config
7. Transition index
8. Other frameworks
9. Troubleshooting

## 1. Next.js setup

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react
```

Keep one config and one `<Ssgoi>` above all route boundaries.

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-provider.tsx
"use client";

import { Ssgoi } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill, slide, zoom } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const productPaths = [
  "/products/all",
  "/products/electronics",
  "/products/fashion",
];

const config = {
  preserveScroll: { exclude: ["/posts/*"] },
  transitions: [
    { on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() },
    {
      ordered: productPaths,
      transition: slide(),
    },
    {
      from: "/gallery",
      to: "/gallery/*",
      transition: zoom({ type: "expand" }),
    },
  ],
};

export function SsgoiProvider({ children }) {
  return <Ssgoi config={config}>{children}</Ssgoi>;
}
```

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { SsgoiProvider } from "./ssgoi-provider";

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        <main className="relative z-0 min-h-dvh overflow-x-clip">
          <SsgoiProvider>{children}</SsgoiProvider>
        </main>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

This layout shell is the first structural requirement. When a route boundary
unmounts, SSGOI temporarily reinserts the detached outgoing DOM node with
`position: absolute` so its OUT animation can finish over the incoming page:

- `relative`: gives the OUT page the correct containing block.
- `z-0`: creates a local stacking context above the shell background.
- `overflow-x-clip`: prevents horizontal overflow during slide, drill, and
  similar transitions.

Put these classes on the element around `<Ssgoi>`, not on each route boundary.

## 2. Route boundaries and React lifetime

SSGOI does not replace the router and does not initiate route unmounts. A React
route boundary is a keyed DOM element with a transition id:

```tsx
<div key={boundary.key} data-ssgoi-transition={boundary.id}>
  {children}
</div>
```

- A changed `key` makes React remove the old subtree and mount a new one.
- `data-ssgoi-transition` identifies that routed region for config matching.
- `<Ssgoi>` observes the real removal/insertion, preserves the detached OUT
  node for its exit animation, and animates the new IN node.

The boundary component can remain mounted in a common layout while its keyed
DOM child is replaced.

The deprecated `<SsgoiTransition>` component only rendered the transition
attribute. Set the attribute directly in the application boundary.

For a small app, `key` and id can both be the pathname. For persistent layouts,
do not make every layout choose an ad hoc key. Define route ownership once and
let consumers pass a semantic `name`:

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-route-boundary.tsx
"use client";

import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { usePathname, useSelectedLayoutSegments } from "next/navigation";

type BoundaryName = "app-shell" | "main-content" | "project-content";
type BoundaryIdentity = { id: string; key: string };

const INTERCEPTION_PREFIX = /^(?:\(\.\.\.\)|\(\.\.\)|\(\.\))+/;

function isRouteGroup(segment: string) {
  return segment.startsWith("(") && segment.endsWith(")");
}

function pathFromSegments(segments: string[]) {
  const path = segments
    .filter((segment) => !isRouteGroup(segment))
    .map((segment) => segment.replace(INTERCEPTION_PREFIX, ""))
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join("/");

  return path ? `/${path}` : null;
}

function resolveBoundary(
  name: BoundaryName,
  pathname: string,
  segments: string[],
): BoundaryIdentity {
  const ownedRoute = pathFromSegments(segments) ?? pathname;

  switch (name) {
    case "app-shell": {
      const routeGroup = segments.find(isRouteGroup);
      if (routeGroup === "(main)") {
        return { id: ownedRoute, key: "main-shell" };
      }

      const project = ownedRoute.match(/^\/projects\/[^/]+/)?.[0];
      return { id: ownedRoute, key: project ?? ownedRoute };
    }
    case "project-content": {
      const project = pathname.match(/^\/projects\/[^/]+/)?.[0];
      const child = pathFromSegments(segments);
      const id = project
        ? child
          ? `${project}${child}`
          : project
        : ownedRoute;
      return { id, key: id };
    }
    case "main-content":
      return { id: ownedRoute, key: ownedRoute };
  }
}

export function SsgoiRouteBoundary({
  children,
  name,
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
  name: BoundaryName;
}) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const segments = useSelectedLayoutSegments("children");
  const boundary = resolveBoundary(name, pathname, segments);

  return (
    <div key={boundary.key} data-ssgoi-transition={boundary.id}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}
```

`BoundaryName` and `resolveBoundary` are application code, not
`@ssgoi/react` API. A name owns both the route id and its React-key partition:

- Reuse a key only while that exact persistent shell should remain mounted.
- Return a different key when navigation leaves the shell.
- A constant key is safe only when the router itself removes the whole
  boundary outside its route layout.
- Put one `app-shell` boundary in the common app layout. Add child names only
  for routed regions that change while the parent remains mounted.

A public `scope(pathname)` callback can express the same mapping, but it is a
low-level application pattern, not SSGOI API. Prefer names so one resolver owns
the route policy.

## 3. Persistent layouts

The common app boundary can span main, detail, and standalone routes:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx — replace the provider line from section 1.
<SsgoiProvider>
  <SsgoiRouteBoundary name="app-shell">{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
</SsgoiProvider>
```

A persistent child layout owns only the content boundary below its stable
header, tabs, or navigation:

```tsx
export default function MainLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <>
      <SsgoiRouteBoundary name="main-content">{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
      <BottomNav />
    </>
  );
}
```

- Main → main: the app-shell key stays; inner content remounts.
- Main → detail: the app-shell key changes; the nav leaves with it.
- Project tab → project tab: the current project base-path key stays; only a
  project content boundary remounts below its header and tabs.

When nested boundaries change in one DOM mutation, SSGOI uses the outer changed
boundary. A nested boundary owns a transition only while its parent remains
mounted.

## 4. Sliding tabs

Use `ordered` to define direction.

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: [
    {
      ordered: [
        "/projects/acme/overview",
        "/projects/acme/docs",
        "/projects/acme/activity",
      ],
      transition: slide(),
    },
  ],
};
```

Increasing index is forward. Decreasing index is backward.

The tab header belongs outside the named content boundary:

```tsx
<>
  <ProjectTabs />
  <SsgoiRouteBoundary name="project-content">{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
</>
```

## 5. Bottom navigation and route groups

```text
app/
  layout.tsx                 # one SsgoiProvider + named app-shell boundary
  (main)/
    layout.tsx               # content boundary + bottom nav
    page.tsx
    collections/page.tsx
    create/page.tsx
  (detail)/
    photo/[id]/page.tsx
```

```tsx
// app/(main)/layout.tsx
export default function MainLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <>
      <SsgoiRouteBoundary name="main-content">{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
      <BottomNav />
    </>
  );
}
```

- Tab → tab: only inner content remounts; nav stays.
- Tab → detail: the common app-shell boundary remounts; nav leaves with it.
- Detail → tab: the common app shell enters with the nav.

Full pattern: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/bottom-nav.txt

Route groups do not change URLs. During a soft parallel/intercepted route,
`usePathname()` points at the modal URL while the background `children` slot
can remain unchanged. Resolve the background boundary id/key from
`useSelectedLayoutSegments("children")`. In the layout that owns `@modal`,
`useSelectedLayoutSegment("modal") !== null` explicitly reports an active
modal slot. The same URL opened directly selects the detail children slot and
therefore receives a detail key.

## 6. Transition config

```ts
type SsgoiConfig = {
  transitions?: SsgoiTransitionRule[];
  middleware?: (from: string, to: string) => { from: string; to: string };
  preserveScroll?: PreserveScrollOption;
};
```

Rule forms:

```ts
{ on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() }

{ from: "/gallery", to: "/gallery/*", transition: zoom() }

{ ordered: ["/tabs/a", "/tabs/b"], transition: slide() }
```

- `on`: route family. Entering is forward; leaving is backward.
- `from`/`to`: precise pair. Reverse matching is enabled by default.
- `ordered`: direction comes from array order.
- `priority`: higher values win before path specificity.

Path patterns:

- `/posts`: exact path.
- `/posts/*`: exactly one arbitrary segment.
- `/posts/**`: `/posts` and every descendant.

A bare `*` remains a compatibility alias for `/**`. Named single-segment forms
remain supported and rank above a single-segment `*` when rules overlap, but
their names are not captured or exposed.

`transitions` may depend on device context:

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: ({ isMobile }) =>
    isMobile
      ? [{ on: "/posts/**", transition: drill() }]
      : [{ on: "/posts/**", transition: fade() }],
};
```

## 7. Transition index

Use these links for effect-specific options.

- `fade`: unrelated pages and quiet cross-fades. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/fade.txt
- `drill`: list → detail hierarchy. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/drill.txt
- `slide`: ordered tabs and steps. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/slide.txt
- `axis`: sibling destinations with Material-style shared-axis motion. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/axis.txt
- `sheet`: compose, filters, and modal-like routes. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/sheet.txt
- `zoom`: card/image → detail expansion. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/zoom.txt
- `hero`: shared elements with page chrome transitions. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/hero.txt
- `scroll`: vertical sequences and editorial paging. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/scroll.txt
- `strip`: perspective strip flip. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/strip.txt
- `film`: cinematic gallery transition. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/film.txt
- `rotate`: card-like rotation. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/rotate.txt
- `blind`: window-blind reveal. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/blind.txt
- `jaemin`: playful branded transition. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/jaemin.txt

## 8. Other frameworks

### React Router

Use `useLocation()` and nested layout routes:

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();

return (
  <div key={pathname} data-ssgoi-transition={pathname}>
    <Outlet />
  </div>
);
```

### TanStack Router

Use router state and parent routes:

```tsx
const pathname = useRouterState({
  select: (state) => state.location.pathname,
});
```

### SvelteKit

Use `+layout.svelte` for persistent chrome and route pages for inner markers.
Use a keyed block only when the layout must force a new DOM boundary.

```svelte
{#key resolveKey($page.url.pathname)}
  <div data-ssgoi-transition={$page.url.pathname}>
    {@render children()}
  </div>
{/key}
```

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/svelte.txt

### Nuxt / Vue

Use `useRoute()` and `:key="resolveKey(route.path)"`.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/vue.txt

### SolidStart

Put `data-ssgoi-transition` on route roots. Persistent route layouts naturally
keep their outer DOM while child routes replace inner boundaries.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/solid.txt

### Qwik City

Use `useSsgoi(root, { config$ })`. Qwik configs must be QRL factories. Put
transition attributes on route component roots under `<Slot />`.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/qwik.txt

### Angular

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/angular.txt

## 9. Troubleshooting

No animation:

1. Confirm both routes are inside the same `<Ssgoi>`.
2. Confirm outgoing and incoming DOM nodes have transition attributes.
3. Confirm the rule matches both path values.
4. Confirm no pathname-keyed ancestor remounts a persistent inner layout.

Wrong region animates:

1. Find the nearest boundary whose key changed.
2. Keep persistent UI outside the inner boundary.
3. Put UI that must leave inside the outer boundary.
4. Fix that boundary name's resolver so routes in the same shell share a key.

Layout jumps:

1. Add `relative z-0` to the shell around `<Ssgoi>`.
2. Add `overflow-x-clip` for horizontal effects.
3. Give route boundaries a full-height background.

Reference templates:

- Next.js: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/nextjs
- React Router: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/react-router
- TanStack Router: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/tanstack-router
- SvelteKit: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/sveltekit
- Nuxt: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/nuxt
- SolidStart: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/solidstart
- Qwik City: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/qwik
